issues.correct: DDD requires agencies to pass the increased rate funding through to DSPs and DSP Supervisors as a base-wage increase (about $0.46/hr), no later than 3/1/2026, including retroactive pay. Industry guidance adds that the increase cannot be paid as a bonus or used for operating expenses.

issues.fix: Add a mandatory-compliance line: the FY26 DSP/Supervisor pass-through of about $0.46/hr is a base-wage increase, effective 1/1/2026, with a 3/1/2026 deadline. Make sure the DSP ($20.71) and supervisor ($52,000) wages reflect it. Do not treat the increase as margin.

issues.current: "whether these are alternatives or cumulative was not confirmed"; an owner-operator "can fill this role".
issues.correct: N.J.A.C. 10:44A-2.5(a) is cumulative. The licensee or executive director must have all three: (1) a Bachelor's degree; (2) five years of progressive management experience working with people with DD, at least two supervisory at a senior or administrative level; and (3) knowledge of program design, staff development and fiscal standards. The application must demonstrate compliance (10:44A-1.4(c)(1)(iv)).
issues.evidence: 10:44A-2.5(a): "The licensee or the executive director shall have: 1. A Bachelor's degree; 2. Five years of progressive management experience … at least two … supervisory".
issues.fix: Replace the note with: 'Requirements are cumulative (bachelor's degree AND 5 yrs progressive DD management, 2 at a senior/supervisory level, AND program/fiscal knowledge). An owner-operator who lacks any one must hire a qualifying executive director, which changes the $47,500/$95,000 salary line.' Check whether a waiver or variance is available under subchapter 1.

issues.current: Only DDD basic training, first aid and background checks are costed (about $250/mo). Fingerprinting, registry checks and drug testing are 'not verified'.
issues.correct: DDD-approved providers must run staff criminal history checks before hire. DDD's Aug 2026 update lists the other provider obligations: DDD-required training, Central Registry of Offenders and Child Abuse Registry checks, pre-employment and random controlled-substance testing, incident reporting, and driver abstract checks for staff who transport. None of these are itemized as costs. DHS also says 10:44A-2.4(b) codifies pre-hire staff criminal history checks.
issues.evidence: DDD Aug 20, 2026 update lists what Goods & Services vendors are NOT required to do: "pre-employment and random drug testing", registry checks, "drivers abstracts".
issues.fix: Add recurring and startup lines for pre-employment and random drug testing, Central Registry and Child Abuse Registry checks, MVR/driver abstracts for any staff who drive, and criminal-history fingerprinting per hire. Include staff turnover. Also check the physical exam and TB test records for direct service staff, which the 2005 text required; this is not confirmed in the current text.

issues.current: Only the annual financial statement audit is mentioned. The annual Fiscal Sustainability Report is not listed.
issues.correct: Agencies with more than $350,000 in annual combined DDD billing must also file an annual Fiscal Sustainability Report. It is due 120 calendar days after fiscal-year end (about Oct 30 for a state-FY agency), on DDD's template, emailed to DDD.WaiverFinancialReports@dhs.nj.gov. The audit applies at $350,000 or more in combined CCP and Supports Program reimbursement, and it must follow GAAS. The audited statements include a balance sheet, income statement and cash flow statement.
issues.evidence: S8: reports "are due 120 calendar days after the close of each State Fiscal Year – on or about October 30."
issues.fix: Add a compliance task and calendar date for the Fiscal Sustainability Report (template, due date, email). State that the audit must be performed under GAAS. Add this contact to regulators.

issues.current: Training is described as DDD basic training (abuse/neglect prevention and first aid) within 90 days. Hour totals were not verified.
issues.correct: 10:44A-2.7(a) requires, within 90 days of hire: DDD Shifting Expectations, preventing abuse and neglect, ECC first aid and CPR, each with a valid certificate on file. Medication training and demonstrated competency are required before staff give any medication, and the competency check is annual. Specialized training (feeding, mobility, seizures, mental health, behavior support plans) is required within 90 days. 10:44A-2.8(b) requires each specialized training to be completed by at least one person on every shift.
issues.evidence: 10:44A-2.7(b): "Staff shall complete medication training and demonstrate competency prior to administering any medication".
issues.fix: Add CPR, Shifting Expectations, medication training with annual competency, and per-shift specialized training to the training cost basis. Include paid training hours in pre-opening DSP costs. Add the 'at least one trained person per shift' rule to the staffing/schedule task.

issues.current: Payroll tax = FICA 7.65% + NJ UI 2.8%. The employer TDI share is 'not verified and not modeled'.
issues.correct: Other mandatory employer costs are not modeled: federal FUTA (0.6% net on the first $7,000 per employee, which I did not verify against a fetched source) and NJ employer TDI contribution (the rate is experience-based and was not verified). UI at 2.8% is applied to all wages although the 2026 UI base is $44,800. The supervisor ($52,000) and executive director ($95,000) wages exceed that base, so the UI portion is overstated for them.
issues.evidence: NJDOL: UI taxable wage base "increases to $44,800 in 2026 from $43,300"; TDI/FLI base $171,100.
issues.fix: Add FUTA and employer TDI as separate lines. Apply UI only to wages up to $44,800 per employee. Confirm the new-employer UI/TDI rates on the NJDOL/Treasury rate notice. The 2.8% rate is secondary-sourced only.
